extraction.name: Video-MME
extraction.description: Video-MME is the first-ever full-spectrum, Multi-Modal Evaluation benchmark of MLLMs in Video analysis. It comprises 900 videos across various scenarios with 2,700 high-quality multiple-choice questions (3 per video). The dataset spans 6 primary visual domains with 30 subfields, covers short-, medium-, and long-term videos ranging from 11 seconds to 1 hour, and integrates multi-modal inputs including video frames, subtitles, and audios. All videos and annotations are manually collected and curated by expert annotators.

extraction.rai:dataCollection: Videos were manually collected from YouTube across 6 key domains (Knowledge, Film & Television, Sports Competition, Artistic Performance, Life Record, and Multilingual) with 30 fine-grained categories. For each category, videos with varying duration lengths were collected: short (<2 minutes), medium (4-15 minutes), and long (30-60 minutes). Corresponding meta-information such as subtitles (if provided) and audios were also obtained. The resulting dataset consists of 900 videos, including 744 videos with subtitles and all 900 with audios.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Not all videos have subtitles; 744 out of 900 videos have subtitles, while all 900 have audios.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Videos sourced from YouTube spanning 6 visual domains and 30 fine-grained categories, along with their associated subtitles and audio tracks.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: In the subtitle-enabled evaluation setting, subtitles corresponding to the timestamps of the sampled video frames are selected. For instance, if 10 frames are sampled from a video, the 10 subtitles that correspond to the respective timestamps of those frames are selected to ensure accurate coherent synchronization between visual and textual multimodal input.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: A quality review process was conducted: each QA pair was examined by a different annotator to verify clarity of language expression, answerability with logically consistent candidate options, and appropriateness of the correct answer. Text-only questions were provided to Gemini 1.5 Pro to filter out QA pairs answerable without video content. Questions not meeting this criterion were returned to the original annotator for revision. Statistical analysis shows Gemini 1.5 Pro achieves less than 15% accuracy in the text-only setup, confirming robustness of the video content-based requirement.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotators with strong English proficiency and extensive research experience in vision-language learning were recruited. Each annotator thoroughly viewed the entire video, then iteratively created three relevant questions, each accompanied by four candidate options, contributing to a total of 2,700 QA pairs. Questions encompass 12 distinct task types including perception, reasoning, and information synthesis. Each QA pair is designed to be closely tied to the video content. A rigorous manual review process was conducted where each QA pair was examined by a different annotator.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The distribution of options (A/B/C/D) follows a near-uniform distribution (25.1/27.2/25.3/22.4%), ensuring an unbiased evaluation. Certificate length analysis was performed to assess temporal difficulty: median certificate lengths of 26s, 164.7s, and 890.7s for short, medium, and long videos respectively. Gemini 1.5 Pro achieves less than 15% accuracy in the text-only setup, underscoring the robustness of the video content-based requirement.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 3 QA pairs per video (each with 4 candidate options)
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Annotators with strong English proficiency and extensive research experience in vision-language learning. Specific contributors acknowledged include Yu Bai, Fangyuan Liu, Yigeng Jiang, and Zezhong Wu.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Gemini 1.5 Pro was used during quality review to filter out QA pairs that can be answered solely based on textual questions without referencing the video content.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Video-MME aims to advance research in multimodal understanding and contribute to the development of more capable and robust MLLMs. The benchmark highlights the need for improvements in handling longer sequences and multimodal data, shedding light on future MLLM development toward artificial general intelligence.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset has a relatively balanced distribution of video durations. Within the short video category, longer videos occupy a larger portion. For medium-length videos, the duration distribution is more uniform, while long videos exhibit a long-tailed distribution with fewer samples as duration increases. Shorter videos predominantly involve perception-related tasks while longer videos mainly feature reasoning tasks.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark reveals that all MLLMs show a general decline in performance as video duration increases, suggesting limitations in processing longer video sequences. Most open-source models fix the number of input frames (e.g., 8 frames), resulting in excessively sparse information density as video length increases. The availability of datasets with complex temporal reasoning in long videos remains limited.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Video-MME is designed for evaluating (testing/benchmarking) Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) on video understanding tasks. It is applicable to both image-based and video-based MLLMs. The benchmark supports evaluation across multiple modality settings: frames only, frames with subtitles, and frames with audio. It covers diverse task types including perception, reasoning, and information synthesis across varying video durations.
